Official-forecast evidence: DC additions explicitly identified in the retained NERC forecast.
Treatment in this study: Remove and replace the identified increment; test interpolated arrival timing and response association separately.

Official-forecast evidence: DC additions separated from mining and other large-load classes.
Quantitative evidence available: 6.7, 23 and 25 GW at the same years; NERC p.~131. The source already adjusts requested DC load.
Treatment in this study: Remove and replace the DC increment without repeating the source adjustment. Provisional large-load response is separate.

Official-forecast evidence: NERC identifies DC-driven growth; an older PJM report classifies a DC-only subset.
Quantitative evidence available: Classified subset: 11.469 GW by 2035; its exact inclusion in the later NERC forecast is unverified.
Treatment in this study: Subset-removal diagnostic conditional on inclusion, not a complete matched replacement or a bound on all DC growth.

Official-forecast evidence: NERC discusses load requests separately from the member forecast. Original ITP slides distinguish firm forecasts and mixed spot-load scenarios.
Quantitative evidence available: No matched DC-only annual increment. SPP's 2025 ITP scenario has approximately 11 GW spot-load growth, 23\% DC; slides 7, 14--15, 34.
Treatment in this study: Retain official demand. Spot-load totals are not removed as embedded DC growth; additional-load cases are stresses.

Official-forecast evidence: Gold Book explicitly includes Table I-14 large loads; these are not a DC-only category.
Quantitative evidence available: Cumulative existing/future summer impacts: 0.466, 2.005 and 2.567 GW in 2025, 2030 and 2035; printed pp.~9, 12--13, 58--59.
Treatment in this study: Retain official demand. Do not subtract the mixed category or substitute queue requests for a DC forecast.

Official-forecast evidence: The 28 March 2025 final draft states that new step loads are not explicitly modeled; historical base demand and electrification remain.
Quantitative evidence available: Slide 5 identifies this exclusion, not zero total embedded DC demand. NERC pp.~70--71 provide no matched DC-only increment.
Treatment in this study: Retain official demand. Missing DC identification is not treated as zero; additional-load cases are stresses.

Official-forecast evidence: NERC WECC-California has a mixed large-load category; the later CEC preliminary DC forecast uses different timing and coverage.
Quantitative evidence available: NERC p.~149: 4.993 GW through 2035. CEC slides 2--4, 11, 13 describe utility applications, ramping and VEA coverage.
Treatment in this study: Retain official demand. The later CEC forecast is not a verified decomposition of the retained NERC category.
